comparisons.peer_summary: Russia has imposed its own restrictions against non-Russian investors and businesses and proposed additional measures aimed at non-Russian owned businesses.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Goldman Sachs disclose specific operational and legal risks arising from Russia's geopolitical actions and retaliatory measures. Citi explicitly quantifies the financial impact of losing control of its Russian subsidiary (AO Citibank), detailing a $1.6 billion CTA loss and $0.9 billion intercompany liability loss. Goldman Sachs does not provide specific financial quantification in this excerpt but notes the broader regulatory environment, stating that Russia has imposed its own restrictions against non-Russian investors and proposed additional measures aimed at non-Russian owned businesses, which serves as a precursor to the type of operational losses Citi experiences.

sentences.text: In the event of a loss of control of AO Citibank in Russia, Citi would be required to (i) write off its remaining nominal net investment, (ii) recognize a CTA loss of approximately $1.6 billion through earnings and (iii) recognize a loss of $0.9 billion on intercompany liabilities owed by AO Citibank to other Citi entities outside of Russia.
Russia has responded with its own restrictions against investors and countries outside Russia and has proposed additional measures aimed at non-Russian owned businesses.
